summary: Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar. She earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015), where she studied under Kapila Abhayawansa.

Hyakudai Sakamoto (1928–2020) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1953). He held posts at the Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences (~1962–1969), Aoyama Gakuin University (~1969–1998), and the Open University of Japan (~1998–2003).

Hyejeong Choi works in Buddhist studies and archaeology. Supervised by John C. Huntington and taught by Byung-Hyun Choi and others, she completed a PhD at Ohio State University (attested 2015) and was a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1985–1986), and Harvard University (~1989–1992), and trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

Hyoung Seok Ham is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Virginia in 2010 and earned a PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2016) under Madhav M. Deshpande, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and others.

Hywel David Lewis (1910–1992) worked in philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Bangor University (~1929–1933) and Jesus College, Oxford (~1933–1936), he later held a post at Bangor University (~1936–1955) and taught Julius Lipner.

Hürelbaatar Ujeed works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge and serves as Professor and Principle Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.
Hōgetsu (1737–1805) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongyuan and Zuihe, and taught Hokai.
Hōin Yamada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and under Gyōin Hashimoto.
Hōju is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University and KU Leuven, and taught Kyokuga Saeki.

Ian Harris (1952–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Cambridge and Lancaster. He founded the UKABS and held positions at St Martin's College (~1985–2007) and the University of Cumbria (attested 2000–2014), among others.

Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University in 2004 and held a research fellow post at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute (attested 2005).
Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Saitama University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka. He taught Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani.

Ian Reader is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Leeds (~1979–1983). He held posts at Stirling (~1989–1999) and Lancaster (~2003–2008), and taught Jørn Borup.

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeologist who earned a PhD in archaeology from the University of Peshawar in 2007 under Farid Khan and Ihsan Ali. He served as Associate Professor and Chairman at Hazara University.

Ichijo Ogawa is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Otani University (~1955–1959). He held teaching posts at Otani University Junior College (~1967–1974) and Otani University (~1974–2007), and taught Nobuchiyo Kotani.

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Kunio Yanagita. He taught at Tohoku University (~1952–1965) and the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

Ichiro Katayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Komazawa and Otani universities under Kogen Mizuno. He held a post at Komazawa University (1975–2013) and served as board chairman of the Society for the Study of Pali and Buddhist Culture.

Ichisada Miyazaki (1901–1995) was a Sinology and history scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1922–1925) under Jitsuzo Kuwabara. He later held a post at Kyoto University (~1936–1965) and taught Mamoru Tonami.
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) was a linguistics scholar who studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1860–1864) and later served there as a professor (1876–1919).
